miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.question: In Micah 6:8, the Lord requires people to do justice.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.learningObjective: Observe the first requirement in Micah 6:8.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.feedbackCorrect: The verse lists justice as the Lord's first requirement.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the list in Micah 6:8: doing justice is on it.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.hint: Look at the list of what the Lord asks.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.question: In Micah 6:8, tap what a person must practice.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.learningObjective: Identify justice as a practice God requires.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.feedbackCorrect: The list begins with dealing rightly with people.

feedbackWrong.a: That describes how to walk with God, not what to practice.
feedbackWrong.c: That is what to love, not what to practice.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.hint: Look for the first item in the verse's list.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.question: According to Micah 6:7, what does the person imagine offering in huge amounts?
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.learningObjective: Observe the exaggeration of the imagined offerings.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.feedbackCorrect: The exaggeration speaks of animals and oil without measure.

feedbackWrong.a: Doves are not mentioned; the exaggeration is rams and oil.
feedbackWrong.b: Incense does not appear in this question of Micah 6:7.
feedbackWrong.c: The verse speaks of rivers of oil, not counted olives.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.hint: Read the two exaggerations in the verse.

options.d: Thousands of rams and rivers of oil

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.question: Put Micah 6:8 in the order of the text.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.feedbackCorrect: The order follows the verse: declared, required and lived.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with what has already been declared to man.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.hint: The verse begins with what has already been declared.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.question: In Micah 6:8, how must a person walk with their God?
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.learningObjective: Remember how to walk with God.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.feedbackCorrect: Walking this way is living without pride before God.

feedbackWrong.a: Hurry ("apressadamente") is not the way of walking named in the verse.
feedbackWrong.b: Pride ("orgulhosamente") is the opposite of the walk the text asks for.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.hint: Think about the end of the verse's list.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.question: What does Micah 6:8 say that connects to this context?
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.learningObjective: Connect Micah 6:8 to what God has already declared.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.feedbackCorrect: God has already declared the way: a just, kind and humble life.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not treat a big offering as payment.
feedbackWrong.c: God declares what is good; he does not stay silent.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.hint: Look at the list the verse presents.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.question: In Micah 6:6–7, the questions climb from year-old calves to thousands of rams.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.learningObjective: Understand how the imagined offerings grow.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.feedbackCorrect: The sequence grows: from the ordinary to an impossible exaggeration.

feedbackWrong.false: Compare 6:6 with 6:7: the imagined amount grows a lot.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.hint: Compare the offerings mentioned, one after another.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.question: In Micah 6:8, tap the verb that shows what the Lord asks of man.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.learningObjective: Recognize the force of God's request.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.feedbackCorrect: This verb shows it is not a vague suggestion.

feedbackWrong.a: "bom" describes the way, not the verb of the request.
feedbackWrong.b: "declarado" speaks of what was already shown, not the request.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.hint: Look for the verb tied to the Lord in the middle of the verse.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.question: How does Micah 6:8 answer the questions of Micah 6:6–7?
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.learningObjective: Relate the questions about offerings to God's answer.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.feedbackCorrect: God trades the list of offerings for a just and humble life.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not approve this extreme; it gets no positive answer.
feedbackWrong.b: The answer does not raise the amount; it shifts the focus to life.
feedbackWrong.d: Worship without justice is exactly what the answer corrects.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.hint: Compare the list of offerings with the final list.

options.a: Accepts the son as final payment
options.b: Asks for double what was imagined
options.c: Shows a just life, not bigger offerings
options.d: Only orders better worship in the temple

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.question: How does the scene move forward in Micah 6:7–8?
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.learningObjective: Understand the movement from the questions to the answer.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.feedbackCorrect: First the exaggeration, then the extreme question, then the answer.

feedbackWrong.default: The declaration of what is good closes the passage.

options.b: Even the firstborn is considered as an offering
options.c: God declares the life he requires

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.question: In Micah 6:6, with what kind of offering does the person think of coming to the Lord?
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.learningObjective: Remember the offering named in the opening question.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.feedbackCorrect: The question starts with offerings burned on the altar.

feedbackWrong.a: Fasts ("jejuns") do not appear in the verse quoted.
feedbackWrong.b: Songs ("cânticos") are not the offering named in this question.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.hint: Read the second question in the verse.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.question: What links Micah 6:8 to 1 Samuel 15:22?
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, living as God asks is worth more than offerings.

feedbackWrong.b: Quantity is not the center of either text.
feedbackWrong.c: Neither text approves disobedience covered by offerings.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.hint: Compare what God values in the two passages.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.question: According to Micah 6:8, ever-bigger offerings are enough to please God without a changed life.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.learningObjective: Evaluate the reading that trades life for offerings.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.feedbackCorrect: God asks for daily practice, not the size of an offering.

feedbackWrong.true: God's answer is a just and humble life, not a bigger offering.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.hint: Notice whether verse 8 talks about offerings or a way of living.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.question: In Micah 6:11, tap what exposes the deceit in the people's trading.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.learningObjective: Support the charge of deceit with the text.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.feedbackCorrect: The deceit shows up in the instruments used for weighing.

feedbackWrong.a: That speaks of the one who weighs, not the deceitful instrument.
feedbackWrong.c: Bags alone don't show the deceit; the set named starts earlier.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.hint: Look for the instruments named in the verse.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.question: What reading does Micah 6:8 support about pleasing God?
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.feedbackCorrect: Pleasing God appears as a life lived with people and with him.

feedbackWrong.a: Humility is part of the walk required, not a minor detail.
feedbackWrong.c: The text says to love this value, not to treat it as optional.
feedbackWrong.d: Impressing with cost is the idea the questions push to the extreme.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.hint: Look at the three verbs in the final answer.

options.a: Separate worship from life with people
options.b: Live with justice, kindness and humility

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.question: Which sequence reveals the meaning of Micah 6:8 in the Bible?
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.learningObjective: See Micah 6:8 within a larger biblical thread.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.feedbackCorrect: The path runs from the Old Testament message to the teaching of Jesus.

feedbackWrong.default: Start in Micah and end with the teaching of Jesus.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.hint: Follow the order of the books named in the pieces.

options.a: Israel asks how to come before God
options.b: God declares justice, mercy and humility
options.c: Jesus presses the weightier matters of the Law

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.question: In Micah 6:8, what must a person love besides doing justice?
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.learningObjective: Remember the value God commands us to love.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.feedbackCorrect: The text joins doing right with loving what is good for others.

feedbackWrong.b: Self-interest ("vantagem") is not the value God commands us to love.
feedbackWrong.c: Indifference ("indiferença") is the opposite of the love the verse asks.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.hint: It is the second item on the final list.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.question: What links Micah 6:8 to Hosea 6:6?
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.learningObjective: Connect Micah's requirement to God's desire in Hosea.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.feedbackCorrect: Both texts put faithful kindness above ritual.

feedbackWrong.b: Neither text excuses us from walking with God.
feedbackWrong.c: Hosea does not approve sacrifice without this central value.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senh.hint: Look for the value the two passages share.

options.a: God wants mercy, not just sacrifice
options.b: God excuses us from walking with him
options.c: Ritual is enough without faithful kindness

estudo:miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senhor-req.context: God reminds the people of his righteous acts in the past. Then come questions about how to come before him, with ever-bigger offerings, until the clear answer of what he requires.
estudo:miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senhor-req.focusQuestion: How can you practice justice and mercy in a choice this week?
estudo:miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senhor-req.keywordGloss: Loving mercy is valuing goodness and forgiveness in how you treat people, as God asks.
facts: God calls the people to remember his righteous acts from Shittim to Gilgal.
The person asks what to bring before the Lord and whether to come with burnt offerings.
The question exaggerates, imagining thousands of rams and ten thousand rivers of oil.
The Lord requires doing justice, loving mercy and walking humbly with God.
God denounces treasures of wickedness and the short measure in the house of the wicked.
